title: Revisão 2 · Dia a Dia: By Accident, On Purpose & On Time

vocab.ex: I deleted your file by accident.
He ignored my message on purpose.
The train arrived right on time.
We got to the gate just in time.
By the time we arrived, the movie had started.
I travelled to Portugal on my own.
She fixed the computer all by herself.
I usually go to work by subway.
They went to the beach by bus.
The bakery is close, so let's go on foot.
I sent the wrong file because I was in a hurry.
They cancelled the trip at the last minute.

expressions.example: I broke the cup by accident, not on purpose!
Please make sure you arrive on time.
We arrived at the airport just in time.

expressions.expr: by the time I got there
expressions.example: By the time I got there, everyone had left.

sentences: I am so sorry! I deleted your presentation file by accident.
He didn't forget to call you — he ignored your message on purpose.
The train leaves at 8:00 sharp, so please arrive on time.
By the time we arrived at the cinema, the movie had already started.
When I first travelled to Portugal, I went completely on my own.
I usually go to work by subway, or I walk on foot.

grammar.title: Expressões Naturais do Dia a Dia
rules: Diga sempre "by accident" (sem querer) e "on purpose" (de propósito).
"On time" significa pontualmente no horário; "in time" significa a tempo.
"By the time" conecta um momento no passado ou futuro a algo que já tinha acontecido.
Meios de transporte usam BY (by subway, by car), mas "a pé" é sempre ON foot.
